expert_role: AEC technology analyst who evaluates design software. I reviewed P17 round 2 (revise-r1) against live vendor, City of Vancouver, competition and course-repo pages on 21 Oct 2026, this time with web search available.

findings.issue: access_for_vtc_team says UNKNOWN and the analysis list is kept as 'general knowledge, not citable'. Autodesk's own Forma blog (1 Nov 2024) says 'Students and educators get Forma for free', with a one-click sun study and 'noise, wind, and embodied carbon'. Search results for Autodesk's education page describe a free named-user seat on a renewable 1-year subscription that needs a school email. The product appears to be rebranded 'Forma Site Design' and there is a 30-day trial. Forma is the closest incumbent and probably the easiest free wind and sun route for a UBC team, so the packet currently steers entrants away from it.
findings.fix: Add the blog as a source (http://blogs.autodesk.com/forma/2024/11/01/architecture-student-projects-with-autodesk-forma/). Set access to 'FREE for students and educators (vendor statement); eligibility terms to be confirmed by a logged-in team member'. Move sun, wind, noise and embodied carbon from unverified_claims into what_it_does as vendor-stated. Keep daylight, microclimate and supertall validity UNVERIFIED. Record the 'Forma Site Design' name and the 30-day trial as seen in search results only.

findings.issue: Step 1b, step 0 and the UNVERIFIED flag name the 'View Protection Guidelines' as a governing input. Council minutes and reports of 10 July 2024 (council.vancouver.ca/20240710) and the City's guideline index say Council repealed the 1989 View Protection Guidelines and approved new Public Views Guidelines (guidelines.vancouver.ca/guidelines-public-views.pdf). The new set removed 14 of 38 views and amended 11, which fits the 24 records now in the open-data set. City search snippets for the Higher Buildings Policy Review also say the protected views approved in July 2024 'will be maintained and continue to guide where higher buildings may be considered'. That partly answers the packet's open question about which document governs.
findings.fix: Replace 'View Protection Guidelines' with 'Public Views Guidelines (Council-approved 10 July 2024; replaced the 1989 VPG)' in steps 0, 1b and 7b and in the flags. Add the Public Views Guidelines PDF and the City Higher Buildings Policy Review page as sources, marked opened:false (403). Say that the 24-record dataset matches the 2024 view set. Keep the height rules UNVERIFIED until a person opens the PDF.

findings.issue: stops_at, license_cost and access_for_vtc_team say 'no student offer found' and that a 4-person team needs four accounts or a paid plan. Snaptrude's own pages (snaptrude.com/students; blog 13 Nov 2025, updated 22 Jun 2026) offer a free Student Plan: full professional features, unlimited projects, real-time collaboration, 120 AI credits a year, a 1-year renewable licence verified by school email, educational use only, workspace ready in 24-48 h.
findings.fix: Correct the three fields and the notes summary. Add snaptrude.com/students and /blog/free-student-plan as sources. Flag that 'educational use only' may conflict with a competition that carries prize money (UNVERIFIED; ask Snaptrude). Record that the earlier /education 404 was the wrong URL.

findings.issue: The course rule asks every result to separate what code, AI and people decide. Each step has only one field, automatable_or_judgment, which puts deterministic code and LLM assistance in the same 'automatable' bucket. For example, step 0 calls brief-contradiction checking automatable, but demo D shows it is an LLM helper whose answer varies between runs, unlike an FSR calculation.
findings.fix: Replace automatable_or_judgment with three fields per step, decided_by_code, assisted_by_ai and decided_by_people, each with one line and a source or a team-assumption label. Do the same for ai_opportunity and ai_wont_improve in the case studies where the engine (code) and the LLM are mixed (TestFit MCP, Infrared).

findings.issue: The cultural and reconciliation step carries 30% of the jury weight, yet its input says no source was opened. That breaks the cite-every-result rule on the most heavily weighted narrative step. A primary municipal source exists: the City of Vancouver UNDRIP Strategy, adopted 25 Oct 2022 and developed with the Musqueam, Squamish and Tsleil-Waututh Nations, with 79 calls to action and a 2024-2028 Action Plan endorsed 25 Jun 2024.
findings.fix: Add the UNDRIP Strategy (council.vancouver.ca/20221025/documents/p1.pdf) and the Nations' own published sites as inputs. Label them sources the team reads, not data the tool interprets. Keep interpretation and any engagement as human-only.

verdict: Round 2 is a large and honest improvement. Most r1 items are fixed, the derived numbers check out (11,468 m2, 103,200 m2, 40 days, 15:59 Pacific), and the reviser was right to reject the r1 critic's Infrared claim. It still fails the gate on facts an entrant would act on. Autodesk Forma is free for students and educators and has vendor-stated sun, wind and noise analyses, yet the packet calls its access unknown. Snaptrude has a free Student Plan. SimScale offers competition sponsorship. Step 1b cites the View Protection Guidelines, which the 2024 Public Views Guidelines replaced. The cultural step has no sources, the code/AI/people split is missing, and time shares are still unmeasured. All of these can be fixed in one short revision.
